content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published updated consolidated guidelines on the treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) in 2022, specifically outlined in Module 4. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for managing multidrug-resistant and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB). The document is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-006312-9 and 978-92-4-006313-6. The publication is protected under a Creative Commons license, allowing non-commercial use, redistribution, and adaptation, provided proper citation is given. The guidelines were developed through collaborative efforts involving experts from various specialties, including public health policy, TB program management, and clinical care for DR-TB and MDR-TB patients. The recommendations were formulated during multiple meetings of the Guideline Development Group (GDG) and subsequently consolidated into the current module. WHO acknowledges the contributions of all individuals and organizations involved in the development of these guidelines. The 2022 update includes new recommendations for the treatment of MDR/RR-TB, such as the 6-month BPaLM regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and moxifloxacin) and a 9-month all-oral regimen. It also addresses longer regimens for MDR/RR-TB, treatment for rifampicin-susceptible but isoniazid-resistant TB (Hr-TB), monitoring patient response using culture, initiating antiretroviral therapy in patients on MDR/RR-TB regimens, and the role of surgery in MDR/RR-TB treatment. Research gaps and areas for further investigation are also highlighted. The guideline development process was led by Fuad Mirzayev, with support from Medea Gegia, Linh Nguyen, and Samuel Schumacher, under the guidance of Matteo Zignol and Tereza Kasaeva, Director of the WHO Global Tuberculosis Programme (WHO/GTB). The GDG was chaired by Holger J. Schünemann and Jeremiah Muhwa Chakaya, with members including clinicians, researchers, and program managers from various countries and institutions. WHO also acknowledges the contributions of the External Review Group (ERG), evidence reviewers, and observers who provided technical input and feedback. The guidelines were funded by grants from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).
